item.description:
​
when planet soul released “set u free” in october 1995, it ushered in the last freestyle wave (to date) at US top 40 radio. the song was a hybrid of new york house and contemporary freestyle music but as if it had been produced on planet mars. the independently released song took off at radio eventually peaking inside the pop top 30 on billboard’s hot 100 in late january 1996. what followed was a flood of songs inspired by the planet soul sound, some more notable than others. one of them was lina santiago’s “feel so good (show me your love).”

written and produced by LA-based di juanito, “feels so good” was initially promoted to radio and club DJs via independent label groove nation records in late1995 before being getting a major label release by universal records. featuring vocals by 17 year old lina santiago, the song was an immediate regional hit outselling major pop artists in the los angeles market upon its official major label release in january 1996. in just a few months, “feels so good” was a bonafide national hit. the song would go on to peak at No. 6 the dance chart, No. 63 on the r&b chart and No. 35 on the hot 100 in april 1996.

the one-two punch success of “set u free” and “feels so good” helped pave the way for a short-lived freestyle resurgence that opened doors for artists such as jocelyn enriquez, rockell, and angelina to score national charting hits.

this was an exciting time for me and other pop music fans who were just (re)discovering freestyle music. loving a genre that did not have the same mainstream and “cool” social capital as hip-hop and alternative rock, made connecting with other freestyle music fans feel even more communal. and that was, at least for me, even more special. one could say, it felt so good!
